title: Working-capital normalization and cash-release sensitivity
prompt:
Prepare a June 30 working-capital normalization using invoice- and bill-level accounting data.

Begin with the working-capital request in `Requests/`. Locate the current AR roll-forward, AP cutoff workpaper, controller collection notes, June close tracker, and the posted P&L/subledger populations. Use the contractor-accounting MCP for LTM revenue, LTM cost of revenue, open AR, retainage, invoice dates, open AP, due dates, and payment holds. Reconcile each population and resolve source status from cutoff and internal labels rather than from filenames alone. Define `ar_over_90` using invoice age strictly greater than 90 days at June 30, rather than days past due. Define `overdue_ap` as bills with due dates strictly before June 30; a bill due on June 30 is not overdue at that cutoff. Calculate DSO as gross open AR divided by LTM revenue times 365 and DPO as gross open AP divided by LTM cost of revenue times 365.

Then calculate the cash release from a five-day DSO improvement plus a three-day DPO extension, using the respective LTM daily run rates. Report the underlying balances, aging/hold populations, ratios, and both components of cash release. Do not change collection dates, release held AP, or edit files.

Return only one JSON object in your final response with exactly these keys: `ltm_revenue`, `ltm_cost_of_revenue`, `gross_open_ar`, `retainage`, `ar_over_90`, `gross_open_ap`, `held_ap`, `overdue_ap`, `net_ar_less_ap`, `dso`, `dpo`, `five_day_dso_cash_release`, `three_day_dpo_cash_release`, `total_cash_release`. Use dollar values to two decimals, ratios and percentages as decimal ratios to at least four decimals (for example, return 0.1863 for 18.63%), and dates as YYYY-MM-DD.
